title: Continuous output watermarking and adaptive per-chunk sampling for streaming observability
creator: Ava Kim
description: Introduce a lightweight per-chunk provenance watermark and adaptive sampling policy to improve streamed-response observability while keeping telemetry costs and PII risk low. This ticket defines the data model, tracing span handoff pattern between progressive chunks, and a redaction-first telemetry pipeline that supports deterministic sampling and replay for debugging failed requests.
acceptance_criteria: A compact watermark structure is emitted with every stream chunk that can be correlated to the request-level trace without including whole prompt/response payloads
Tracing spans are produced for chunk generation, KV cache hits, and outbound tool calls with stable span IDs and a documented handoff mechanism
Adaptive sampling reduces telemetry volume by >= 5x on high-throughput tenants while preserving >= 95% of unique error cases for replay
Redaction rules are applied before any telemetry leaves the serving node; sampled payloads for debugging are stored only after consented retention policy
Grafana + Honeycomb dashboards show per-chunk latency percentiles, watermark lag, sample rate, and redaction success rate for two weeks
tasks: Design compact watermark schema (8-12 fields) describing chunk offsets, kv-cache anchors, model variant and truncated token ranges
Define span handoff policy: parent span at request start, child spans for chunk frames, and deterministic continuation IDs for client-side reassembly
Implement adaptive sampler service that uses token-rate and error-signals to decide per-request sampling budget
Integrate redaction library into stream telemetry hotpath with allowlist/denylist rules and bloom-filter based PII markers
Add end-to-end tests that replay sampled traces and verify redact-before-export behavior
Create dashboards and an alert: sample-rate-drift > 2x baseline and redaction-fail-rate > 0.1%
decisions: Use a compact watermark (no raw text/prompt) to enable low-cost correlation between chunks and the parent request
Store full sampled payloads only in a review-mode bucket with strict KMS encryption and 30-day TTL
Adopt a deterministic continuation ID format (request-key + chunk-index + salted-hash) to simplify client/server reassembly without embedding raw prompts
Perform redaction at the SGX-like serving layer (fast, pre-export) rather than downstream to minimize PII exposure surface
Prefer bloom-filter PII detection for speed and memory footprint but keep an opt-in exact-detector for enterprise debugging
tradeoffs: Minimal watermark reduces telemetry size but sometimes requires extra correlation queries when user-level metadata is scarce
Aggressive sampling saves cost but increases time-to-detect rare model regressions; mitigated by an error-triggered sampling override
Pre-export redaction prevents PII leakage but may obscure context for root-cause analysis; solution: gated full-payload retention with access controls
Deterministic continuation IDs simplify tracing but leak a stable identifier across logs; mitigated by per-tenant salt rotation

Load test at 10x baseline token-rate to validate telemetry pipeline backpressure handling

rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag behind runtime-config for per-tenant opt-in; rollout to internal and dev tenants

Phase 2: Increase to 25% with sampler thresholds tuned, add Console visibility for chunk-level charts
Phase 3: Global enable with enterprise opt-outs and retention gating; deprecate legacy chunk-provenance fields
